subject: Re: Scheduling demo — timezone/UTC-offset edge case (Sydney/Tokyo)
messages:
From: Samantha Lau <samantha.lau@brightretail.sg>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:18:00 +08:00
Subject: Demo — availability (APAC hours)

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the quick reply earlier. We're excited to see Redwood in action. For context, our core ops team is in Singapore (SGT, UTC+8); a few stakeholders will dial in from Tokyo (JST, UTC+9) and one site lead in Sydney (AEST, UTC+10).

Preferred windows (local):
- Morning SGT: 09:00–11:30
- Early afternoon SGT: 13:30–15:00

Can you do any of the following proposed slots (all local times are SGT/JST/AEST adjustments):
- Wed 2026-07-07 10:00 SGT (11:00 JST / 12:00 AEST)
- Thu 2026-07-08 09:30 SGT (10:30 JST / 11:30 AEST)
- Fri 2026-07-09 23:30 JST (22:30 SGT / 00:30 AEST — we realize this is late for Sydney, but one of our Tokyo folks prefers it)

The last option is the trickiest because 23:30 JST becomes 00:30 in Sydney the next calendar day — just flagging it in case your calendar/ICS conversions treat it differently. Also note our folks are careful around midnight slots.

I've attached a small timezone matrix for clarity.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lau
Head of Platform Ops — Bright Retail
Attachment: timezone-offset-matrix.png (image/png)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>
To: Samantha Lau <samantha.lau@brightretail.sg>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:05:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Demo — availability (APAC hours)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear windows and the matrix, that's helpful.

We can do Wed 2026-07-07 10:00 SGT (11:00 JST / 12:00 AEST) — I'll pencil that in.

Regarding the Fri 23:30 JST option: good catch. We had a past issue where our calendar defaults to UTC for some invites created by our EU-based scheduling bot; that caused one invite to show as the "previous day" in Sydney because the ICS was stamped in UTC and some clients rendered it incorrectly. To avoid that, we'll send an explicit ICS with explicit TZ entries and also include a human-friendly line with all three local times in the invite description.

Monica — can you please create the invite for Wed 2026-07-07 10:00 SGT, set the event timezone to Asia/Singapore, attach the demo runbook, and copy the link to the Redwood demo room? Also please check that the ICS includes VTIMEZONE for Asia/Singapore and that it's not being converted to UTC by our calendar service.

Samantha — once Monica posts the invite, please confirm that the times show correctly in Tokyo and Sydney on your side. If anyone needs an alternate time, we can open Thu 09:30 SGT as backup.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Rafael
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: brightretail-demo.ics (calendar/ics)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
To: Samantha Lau <samantha.lau@brightretail.sg>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo — availability (APAC hours)

Hi all — invite created and attached.

Quick notes on what I did (so you can validate on your side):
- Event set to timezone: Asia/Singapore (TZID: Asia/Singapore in ICS VTIMEZONE block)
- Start: 2026-07-07T10:00:00 Asia/Singapore, Duration: 60 minutes
- Description includes: "Local times — Singapore: 10:00 (SGT, UTC+8) | Tokyo: 11:00 (JST, UTC+9) | Sydney: 12:00 (AEST, UTC+10)"
- Attached: demo runbook (internal), brightretail-demo.ics exported from our calendar, timezone-offset-matrix.png for quick reference

I've also forced the calendar link to use the event's TZ-aware URL: https://calendar.redwood.ai/event/BR-2026-072-demo — please check it in Gmail, Outlook, and Apple Calendar if you can. Different clients behave differently when ICS lacks VTIMEZONE.

Samantha — can you confirm that the invite shows 11:00 for Tokyo and 12:00 for Sydney on your side? If it still appears off, please reply with a screenshot and we'll escalate to platform.

Thanks,
Monica
Senior Customer Success Ops | Redwood Inference
